title: Understanding MSE and MAE
text: When considering Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE), think about how each one treats errors. MSE squares the errors, which means larger errors have a bigger impact. MAE, on the other hand, treats all errors equally. How might this affect the choice of which to optimize for?

title: Convexity of MSE
text: The MSE loss surface is convex, which means it has a single global minimum. This property ensures that there is one optimal value for $$\theta_0$$ that minimizes the MSE. Can you think of why this might be advantageous when building models?
